question.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$*

current_example.problem:
Evaluate
$\displaystyle
\int_{0}^{1} \int_{y}^{1} \int_{0}^{y} 3e^{x^3} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y.$

*Hint: Change change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x.$*
current_example.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
\int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} 3e^{x^3} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: y \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq y \right\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
\int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{0}^{y} 3e^{x^3} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/bdd856ef8a7940a009b7ee27d6614fdb8c042e6655c2316ce4db0633bfd04e9f.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad y \leq x \leq 1 \right\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y = y(x),$ is

$$
x = y \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad y = x
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y = 0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq y \leq x \right\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/1e28e1cef9743da80d6fd2d38840810b12239d8546254c4d4cca767568f76a53.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}{\int }_{0}^{y}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}[{\int }_{0}^{y}\text{d}z]\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}[z]_{0}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3y{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}[{\int }_{0}^{x}y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[{e}^{{x}^{3}}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(e-1).\end{aligned}
$$
